The attempt to portray my remarks as though I called for the dismissal of the Commander of the Central Command during the broadcast is an outright lie, part of a political campaign aimed against the government.

On July 28, Channel 14 News reported that I had accepted the Chief of Staff’s recommendation, and after interviewing Maj. Gen. Bar Kalifa and concluding that he was the most suitable candidate, I decided to advance his appointment in accordance with the established procedures.

During yesterday’s interview, when one of the participants called for “the general to be dismissed,” I responded immediately and clearly: “No.” The exchange was recorded on video and is documented.

In other words, months before the interview, the Chief of Staff’s recommendation had already been made, approved by me, and the appointment process was already underway. Therefore, the attempt to claim that the decision was made as a result of the interview does not stand up to the facts.

This is not a genuine controversy but a media-driven attempt to divert attention from the real question: what would happen if Yair Golan, who has already threatened to dismiss Maj. Gen. David Zini, were to become defense minister in a government led by Gadi Eisenkot. In that case, there is concern that figures associated with the old “conceptzia” (the pre–October 7 security doctrine) would be appointed again, potentially harming Israeli settlements and Israel’s security.

That did not happen under my tenure, and it will not happen.
